### Observed differences

- The successors of A25 changed completely: in the earlier window A25 was followed by A27 in about 99 of 100 observed outgoing transitions; in the later window its transitions split almost evenly among A35, A36 and A41 (about 33% each), with A27 below 1 in 100. [DIR001]
- The successors of A26 changed the opposite way: earlier, A26 was followed by A41 (about 37%), A35 (34%) and A36 (28%); later, A26 is followed by A30 in about 99 of 100 transitions. [DIR002]
- A35, A36 and A41 behave the same internally in both windows — each is followed by one of the other two (about two thirds of transitions combined) or by a single exit activity (about one third) — but that exit changed from A30 (28–37% earlier) to A27 (about 31–35% later), where A30 now accounts for under 1%. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Step distances mirror this: A25 was followed by A27 immediately (distance 1 in 99% of about 200 traces) and later at 4–5 steps (93% at 4); A26 was followed by A30 at 4–5 steps (93% at 4) and later immediately (98% at 1), each with about 200 traces in both windows. [LAG001, LAG003]
- Relations changed sides in aggregate: A26 followed by A35, A36 or A41 within five steps, and each block member followed by A30 within five steps, fell from about 200 traces to 1–2 traces, while A25 followed by A35 and A35 followed by A27 rose from 1 trace to about 199; the profiles on the thin side rest on only 1–2 observations. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
- Relative positions shifted consistently: A35, A36 and A41 now occur earlier (mean relative position about 0.58–0.59 before vs about 0.41 after), while A27 (0.38 vs 0.47) and A26 (0.53 vs 0.62) occur later. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Participation did not change: every activity involved is observed in essentially all 200 traces of both windows, so this is a reordering of existing behaviour, not activities appearing or disappearing. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block A35–A36–A41, executed in a varying internal order, was relocated: in the earlier window A25 led directly to A27 and, later in the trace, A26 led to the block, which then led to A30; in the later window the block runs directly after A25 and before A27, while A26 leads directly to A30. As part of the same rearrangement, A27 moved from immediately after A25 to after the block, and A30 moved from after the block to immediately after A26. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003]

The hypothesis is shown directly by the successor replacements at A25, A26 and the block members, and the distance profiles match a three-activity relocation exactly (A25→A27 from 1 step to 4–5; A26→A30 from 4–5 steps to 1), with about 200 traces behind each key item in both windows; the position shifts agree, and 20 qualifying items against roughly 0.6 expected without change puts the ensemble far beyond what random re-splits produce (each item alone exceeds about 199 of 200 reference comparisons). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Limitations: the exact step distances for pairs observed on only one side rest on 1–2 traces, so those fine-grained distances are weakly supported even though the appearance or near-disappearance of the relations is consistent across items; and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sample a shift in the mix of two process variants rather than a relocation within one process. All position and distance figures are event positions, not clock times, so no timing claim is made. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

Other differences: only sub-1% successor shares appear or disappear (for example A41→A49 or A36→A06 giving way to A36→A22, A23 or A46), which are at noise level and not part of the hypothesis. [DIR004, DIR005]
